title: Retries & Circuit Breakers
intro: Protect downstream dependencies and prevent cascading distributed failures using adaptive retry backoff algorithms and stateful circuit breakers.
objectives: Model the 3 states of a Circuit Breaker: Closed, Open, and Half-Open.
Implement Exponential Backoff with Full Jitter to eliminate retry storms.
Configure fallback responses (cache reads, static defaults) on tripped circuits.
body:
### The Circuit Breaker State Machine
1. **Closed**: Normal operations. Requests pass through to downstream service. Failure count is tracked over a sliding time window.
2. **Open**: If failure rate exceeds threshold (e.g. 50% errors over 10 seconds), the circuit trips to **Open**. All subsequent requests fail fast immediately without hitting downstream, sparing the struggling service.
3. **Half-Open**: After a cooldown sleep window (e.g. 30 seconds), circuit permits a small canary fraction of requests through. If canary calls succeed, circuit resets to **Closed**; if they fail, circuit flips back to **Open**.

### Exponential Backoff with Full Jitter
Retrying immediately upon failure causes **retry storms (thundering herds)**. Always add randomness (jitter):

$$\text{sleep} = \text{random}(0, \min(\text{cap}, \text{base} \times 2^{\text{attempt}}))$$
keyIdea: Fail fast when downstream is drowning. Exponential backoff with jitter prevents retry avalanches; circuit breakers give downstream services breathing room to recover.

concepts.title: Thundering Herd (Retry Storm)
concepts.body: When thousands of client requests retry at the exact same millisecond interval, creating periodic shockwaves that repeatedly knock recovering servers back offline.

concepts.title: Fallback Cache
concepts.body: Returning cached stale data or generic defaults when the circuit is Open, preserving partial user functionality.

examples: Resilience4j and Envoy distributed circuit breaker filters.

quiz.prompt: Why is \'Full Jitter\' added to exponential backoff algorithms?
options: To decorrelate retry timestamps across clients, preventing periodic synchronized traffic spikes (retry storms)
To prioritize mobile clients over desktop clients
quiz.explanation: Jitter spreads out retries evenly over time, preventing synchronized thundering herd spikes on downstream services.
